title.en: US hits dozens of trading partners with new wave of tariffs
title.zh: 美国以强迫劳动为由对数十个贸易伙伴征收关税

summary.en: The United States has imposed tariffs on 60 trading partners, citing concerns that these nations have not adequately addressed forced labor practices within their supply chains.
summary.zh: 美国已对60个贸易伙伴征收关税，理由是这些国家未能充分阻止强迫劳动。

body.en:
The US has imposed new tariffs on 60 trading partners in the latest escalation in the trade war reignited by US President Donald Trump when he returned to office last year.

Those targeted, including the UK, China and the European Union, will face a tariff of 10% to 12.5% on all goods, accounting for almost all American imports.

The tariffs, which replace an identical levy which expires on Friday, are based on claims key economic partners have failed to properly tackle forced labour.

But US trade expert Caroline Freund said the move is "not about forced labour" but that Trump is simply "looking for a legal reason to put the tariffs in".

The US Supreme Court had ruled earlier this year that many of the tariffs imposed globally under emergency powers were illegally enacted.

The 10%-12.5% duties on imports were proposed last month by the White House and over concerns they were not doing enough to tackle forced labour.

"Today's action will begin to correct what is both a human rights abuse and distortive trade practice to improve the welfare of workers everywhere," US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said.

The new duties apply to the top 60 US trade partners covering 99.4% of US imports, it added.

The new tariffs were a "like for like" swap with the regime that expired on Friday, Freund, Dean of the UC San Diego School of Global Policy and Strategy, told the BBC's Today programme.

Asked about the forced labour justification, she said: "I think they were looking for a legal reason to put the tariffs in and that they can maintain them because their goals and Greer has been very clear about this, as has Trump, is about the trade deficit and it is about US manufacturing, it is not about forced labour."

The new levies show the Trump administration is "determined" to push on with its tariff strategy, said trade policy expert Deborah Elms from the Hinrich Foundation.

It is unlikely countries hit with tariffs will be able to prove that they have sufficient measures to prevent forced labour imports, she told the BBC.

The levies are likely to raise costs for businesses and consumers, although its impact could be softened due to the number of exempted goods, said the Asia Society Policy Institute's economic security expert Wendy Cutler.

She added most trading partners would be disappointed with the new levies and were likely to focus on ways to "reduce their dependence on the US" by making deals with other countries.

The head of the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) said the UK had lost its comparative advantage against the European Union as a result of the new tariffs.

William Bain told the BBC the EU has a 10% all-inclusive deal for tariffs on its goods, while the UK is facing 10% universal tariffs on top of any duties imposed on individual...
body.zh: 美国对 60 个贸易伙伴征收新关税，这些贸易伙伴占其进口产品的绝大多数，理由是它们未能妥善制止强迫劳动。 这些关税从 10% 到 12.5% 不等，针对的是主要经济伙伴，包括英国、中国、欧盟、加拿大、日本和印度。今年早些时候对外国商品征收 10% 的临时税已到期，这些措施于周五生效。 此举是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普去年重返办公室后重新引发的全球贸易战的最新升级。 美国最高法院今年早些时候裁定，全球根据紧急权力征收的许多关税都是非法实施的。 上个月，白宫提议对数十个国家的进口产品征收 10%-12.5% 的关税，原因是担心这些国家在解决强迫劳动问题上做得不够。 周四，美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔在特朗普的指导下表示，这些关税现已生效。 他的声明称：“今天的行动将开始纠正侵犯人权和扭曲贸易行为，以改善世界各地工人的福利。” 格里尔援引了 1974 年《贸易法》第 301 条，该条规定美国对给美国商业造成负担或限制的行为进行贸易执法。 本周早些时候，特朗普政府援引另一项法规，即《1930 年关税法》第 338 条，对来自加拿大的产品征收 50% 的关税。 周四，美国贸易代表办公室表示，最新的关税是针对合作伙伴征收的，“因为他们未能实施并有效执行禁止进口强迫劳动生产的商品”。 报告补充称，新关税适用于美国前 60 个贸易伙伴，涵盖美国进口产品的 99.4%。 该办公室表示，特朗普已将禁止进口强迫劳动产品作为与其他国家互惠贸易协定的“关键”部分。 它表示，到目前为止，已有 10 个贸易伙伴同意在这些协议中实施此类禁令，其他国家也已在最近几周针对其调查实施了禁令。 该办公室补充说，“承诺采取并有效执行”强迫劳工进口禁令的贸易伙伴将被征收10%的关税，而那些没有这样做的贸易伙伴将被征收更高的12.5%的关税。 格里尔表示，他“受到贸易伙伴迅速采取行动采取强迫劳工进口禁令的鼓舞，并期待确保其有效执行”。 辛里奇基金会的贸易政策专家黛博拉·埃尔姆斯表示，新的关税表明特朗普政府“决心”继续推行其关税战略。 受到关税打击的国家不太可能证明他们有足够的措施来防止强迫......

reflection.en: The news of tariffs imposed due to forced labor concerns reminds us of the profound injustice when workers are exploited. James 5:4 powerfully states that the cries of unpaid laborers reach Yahweh's ears, highlighting the divine awareness and condemnation of such practices. This serves as a call for all nations and businesses to uphold ethical labor...
reflection.zh: 因强迫劳动问题而征收关税的消息，提醒我们劳工被剥削所带来的严重不公。雅伟书5:4有力地指出，未付工资的工人的呼声已达到雅伟的耳中，这突显了雅伟对这种行为的洞察和谴责。这呼吁所有国家和企业维护道德劳动标准，并保护每个人的尊严。

verse.textEn: Look! The wages you failed to pay the workers who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of Yahweh Almighty.
verse.textZh: 工人给你们收割庄稼，你们亏欠他们的工钱，这工钱有声音呼叫，并且那收割之人的冤声已经入了万军之主的耳了。

reflection.en: The fear expressed by a child after a terror attack highlights how deeply such events can shake our sense of security and belonging. In moments when the world feels unsafe, Yahweh reminds us not to fear, promising His presence and strength to uphold us. This divine assurance offers a steadfast hope amidst the anxieties of life.
reflection.zh: 恐怖袭击后孩子所表达的恐惧，凸显了此类事件如何深刻地动摇我们的安全感和归属感。在世界感到不安全的时候，雅伟提醒我们不要惧怕，应许祂的同在和力量来扶持我们。这份神圣的应许在生活的焦虑中提供了坚定的盼望。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: Donald Trump hits Australian exports to US with new higher trade tariff over claims of ‘forced labour’

When tariffs are imposed based on claims that are disputed as “unjustified,” it highlights the importance of integrity in global commerce. Yahweh delights in just weights and measures, reminding us that fairness should guide all economic...

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.

title.en: India's 'cockroach' protesters and government to hold talks as stalemate continues
title.zh: 印度“蟑螂”抗议者与政府将举行会谈，僵局持续

summary.en: After a 26-day hunger strike, activist Sonam Wangchuk has ended his protest, paving the way for talks between India's government and the 'cockroach' protesters to address the ongoing stalemate.
summary.zh: 在长达26天的绝食抗议后，活动家索南·旺楚克已结束抗议，为印度政府与被称为“蟑螂”的抗议者举行会谈以解决持续的僵局铺平了道路。

body.en:
Representatives of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will hold talks with the government on Friday as thousands of people continue to protest day and night demanding the education minister's resignation.

The meeting follows an eventful night where activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his hunger strike after 26 days of fasting in solidarity with the protests.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi also posted a video promising a tough new law on examination paper leaks, the issue at the core of the protests.

However, CJP spokespersons have said they will continue protesting until minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.

The protests - which have seen tens of thousands of young people participate across the country - have become a major headache for Modi's government, which had tried to ignore them in the first few weeks.

That changed last Saturday, when authorities forcibly removed Wangchuk from the protest site and admitted him to hospital, citing health concerns.

Two days later, police in Delhi cracked down on protesters attempting to march to parliament, leaving scores injured and sparking massive public anger.

Last night, Modi posted a video message - shot vertically, seen as an attempt to reach the young protesters who are active on Instagram - saying that a tough new law on examination paper leaks was being prepared.

He said he had received a draft of the law, which would be discussed by the cabinet on Friday before being finalised and introduced in parliament.

Exam paper leaks are at the centre of the controversy - India has witnessed dozens of them over the past couple of decades. The latest trigger was the leak of the question paper for the medical entrance exam, National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET).

Nearly 2.28 million candidates sat the exam on 3 May. It was cancelled days later, and a re-test was held . More than 20 students have reportedly died by suicide since the cancellation, with some of their family members also joining the protest.

While Modi did not address the protests directly, he said he was "well aware that the issue of paper leaks is not a small matter".

"It causes immense distress to [hundreds of thousands] of students and their parents," he said, reiterating his earlier promise to strengthen the legal framework to punish culprits.

But the CJP's response suggested they would not back down on the demand for Pradhan's resignation.

"The fact that Modi had to make a selfie [video] at midnight shows the pressure he's under. He has promised to take action - the best he can do is sack his education minister," CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka told the BBC from the protest site.

Wangchuk said that he was ending his hunger strike after the government assured him no legal action would be taken against protesters at Jantar Mantar,...
body.zh: 印度蟑螂简塔党（CJP）的代表将于周五与政府举行会谈，数千人日夜继续抗议，要求教育部长辞职。 在这次会议之前，活动家索南·旺楚克 (Sonam Wangchuk) 在经历了 26 天的禁食声援抗议活动后结束了绝食抗议。 总理纳伦德拉·莫迪还发布了一段视频，承诺针对试卷泄露问题制定严厉的新法律，这是抗议活动的核心问题。 然而，CJP 发言人表示，他们将继续抗议，直到部长达门德拉·普拉丹 (Dharmendra Pradhan) 辞职为止。 全国各地有数以万计的年轻人参加了抗议活动，这已成为莫迪政府的一大头疼问题，莫迪政府在最初几周内试图忽视这些抗议活动。 上周六，情况发生了变化，当局以健康问题为由，强行将旺楚克带离抗议现场，并将他送进医院。 两天后，德里警方镇压了试图游行至议会的抗议者，造成数十人受伤，并引发了巨大的公众愤怒。 昨晚，莫迪发布了一段垂直拍摄的视频信息，被视为试图接触 Instagram 上活跃的年轻抗议者，称正在准备一项针对试卷泄露的严厉新法律。 他表示，他已收到该法律草案，该草案将于周五由内阁讨论，然后最终确定并提交议会。 试卷泄露是争议的焦点——过去几十年来，印度发生了数十起试卷泄露事件。最新的触发因素是医学入学考试、全国资格暨入学考试（NEET）试卷的泄露。 5月3日，近228万名考生参加了考试。几天后取消了，并进行了重新测试。据报道，自取消活动以来已有 20 多名学生自杀身亡，他们的一些家人也加入了抗议活动。 虽然莫迪没有直接回应抗议活动，但他表示，他“很清楚文件泄露问题不是一个小问题”。 他说：“这给[数十万]学生及其家长带来了巨大的痛苦。”他重申了他早些时候的承诺，即加强惩罚罪犯的法律框架。 但 CJP 的回应表明，他们不会放弃普拉丹辞职的要求。 CJP 发言人阿舒托什·兰卡 (Ashutosh Ranka) 在抗议现场对 BBC 表示：“莫迪不得不在午夜自拍（视频），这表明了他所承受的压力。他已承诺采取行动，他能做的最好的事情就是解雇他的教育部长。” 旺楚克表示，在政府向他保证不会对简塔·曼塔天文台的抗议者采取法律行动后，他将结束绝食抗议。

reflection.en: In situations of deep disagreement, the path to resolution often begins with a willingness to engage in dialogue. This verse reminds us of the personal responsibility to pursue peace, even when challenges persist. May these talks be guided by a spirit of mutual respect and a sincere desire for understanding.
reflection.zh: 在深刻分歧的局面中，解决之道往往始于对话的意愿。这节经文提醒我们，即使挑战依然存在，我们也有责任去追求和平。愿这些会谈在相互尊重的精神和真诚理解的愿望下进行。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: ‘A small snippet’: what pubs make of Burnham’s £100m rates giveaway
title.zh: “一小部分”：酒吧如何看待伯纳姆的1亿英镑税率减免

summary.en: Andy Burnham, as prime minister, has announced a 20% reduction in business rates for pubs, clubs, and live music venues. However, landlords in the hospitality sector express concern that the high operating costs of their businesses may still outweigh the potential savings from this discount.
summary.zh: 安迪·伯纳姆作为首相，宣布将酒吧、俱乐部和现场音乐场所的商业税率降低20%。然而，酒店业的业主们表示，高昂的运营成本可能仍然会抵消这项折扣带来的潜在节省。

body.en:
One of Andy Burnham’s first policy measures as prime minister is a 20% reduction in business rates for pubs, clubs and live music venues.

The policy, announced on Thursday, is part of a broader agenda to support the high street and will cost £100m.

So how does the policy measure up in the context of running a business and where does the money on your bar bill actually go? Also, can the rates reduction halt a trend in pub closures, running at about one a day ?

The Red Lion serves 15 types of pie, 15 types of potato side dish, 15 types of veg and 15 types of gravy but the most common order is a steak and ale pie with chips, cauliflower cheese and onion gravy, washed down with a pint of Bass.

“Over the course of a week, we’d sell about 300 of them and get through about six 25kg sacks of potatoes from a farmer up the road. A local brewery does our own beer, the Pie & Glory, but the Bass is our most popular.”

Smith says he used to pay no business rates at all thanks to relief provided for rural businesses. Now he pays about £680 a year and has already seen his estimated bill oscillate several times because of successive policy tweaks, including a nationwide property revaluation.

Business rates account for about 16p of a pie and a pint, he reckons, compared with VAT of £3.42.

“I’m not going to knock it [the business rate cut], it’s showing willing from Mr Burnham. But it’s a small snippet,” says Smith.

He supports a hospitality-wide campaign to cut VAT from 20% to 10%, a measure that Burnham supported when he was mayor of Manchester. That could cost the Treasury an estimated £10bn.

Ingredients: £6.48 VAT: £3.42 Staff: £3.88 Employer’s taxes: £0.74 Utility bills, operating costs and mortgage: £2.85 Business rates: £0.16

Packed House is a family-run consultancy that acts as a commercial director for independent hospitality businesses and provides a breakdown of annual costs for businesses with a turnover of about £1m.

Colm O’Leary, the director at Packed House, says: “We help owners who are overworked and underpaid build profitable and successful businesses.”

Costs include high rates of duty paid on alcohol that pubs buy in. Staffing costs include national minimum wage and national insurance contributions, both of which have gone up under Labour.

The estimate shows why some hospitality bosses have given only a lukewarm reception to the business rates relief package, given the scale of other costs they are facing.

The amount paid depends on the type and location of premises, but O’Leary says £5,000 would not be unusual for a business with a turnover of £1m. That means a saving from the policy of about £1,000, in line with what the government has said pubs could save.

body.zh: 安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 作为总理的首批政策措施之一是将酒吧、俱乐部和现场音乐场所的营业费降低 20%。 该政策于周四宣布，是支持商业街的更广泛议程的一部分，耗资 1 亿英镑。 那么，在经营企业的背景下，这项政策的效果如何？酒吧账单上的钱实际上去了哪里？此外，利率的降低能否阻止酒吧关闭的趋势，即每天大约关闭一家酒吧？ Red Lion 提供 15 种馅饼、15 种土豆配菜、15 种蔬菜和 15 种肉汁，但最常见的订单是牛排和麦芽酒馅饼，配薯条、花椰菜奶酪和洋葱肉汁，配上一品脱鲈鱼。 “在一周的时间里，我们卖出了大约 300 个土豆，并从路边农民那里买了大约 6 袋 25 公斤重的土豆。当地一家啤酒厂生产我们自己的啤酒 Pie & Glory，但 Bass 是我们最受欢迎的啤酒。” 史密斯说，由于为农村企业提供了救济，他过去根本不需要支付任何商业税。现在，他每年支付约 680 英镑，并且由于连续的政策调整（包括全国范围内的房地产重估），他的预估账单已经多次波动。 他估计，一个馅饼和一品脱的商业税率约为 16 便士，而增值税为 3.42 英镑。 “我不会反对（企业降息），这表明了伯纳姆先生的意愿。但这只是一小部分，”史密斯说。 他支持一项将增值税从 20% 削减至 10% 的酒店业运动，伯纳姆在担任曼彻斯特市长时也支持这项措施。这可能会让财政部损失约 100 亿英镑。 原料：6.48 英镑 增值税：3.42 英镑 员工：3.88 英镑 雇主税：0.74 英镑 水电费、运营成本和抵押贷款：2.85 英镑 商业费率：0.16 英镑 Packed House 是一家家族经营的咨询公司，担任独立酒店企业的商务总监，为营业额约为 100 万英镑的企业提供年度成本明细。 Packed House 总监科尔姆·奥利里 (Colm O’Leary) 表示：“我们帮助那些工作过度、工资过低的业主建立盈利且成功的企业。” 成本包括对酒吧购买的酒类征收高额关税。员工成本包括国家最低工资和国家保险缴款，这两项费用在工党执政期间都上涨了。 这一估计表明，考虑到一些酒店业老板面临的其他成本规模，他们对营业费减免方案反应冷淡。 支付的金额取决于经营场所的类型和位置，但奥利里表示，对于营业额为 100 万英镑的企业来说，5,000 英镑并不罕见。这意味着该政策可节省约 1,000 英镑，与政府所说的酒吧可以节省的金额一致。 “这一政策决定的速度是一个积极的信号，但好处是......

reflection.en: Running a business, especially in the hospitality sector, involves careful planning and significant effort to navigate high operating costs. This news reminds us that while human policies aim to help, true stability and the establishment of our endeavors ultimately rest in committing our work to Yahweh. Even with challenges, we can trust that Yahweh sees...
reflection.zh: 经营企业，尤其是在酒店业，需要周密的计划和巨大的努力来应对高昂的运营成本。这则新闻提醒我们，尽管人类的政策旨在提供帮助，但我们事业的真正稳定和建立最终在于将我们的工作交托给雅伟。即使面临挑战，我们也可以相信雅伟看到我们的劳苦，并帮助我们成就计划。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Families still search for bodies a month after Venezuela earthquakes
title.zh: 委内瑞拉地震一月后，家庭仍在搜寻遗体

summary.en: Officials in Venezuela report that a month after devastating earthquakes, the death toll has exceeded 5,300, with estimates of missing persons potentially reaching 50,000 as families continue their search for loved ones.
summary.zh: 委内瑞拉官员表示，在毁灭性地震发生一个月后，死亡人数已超过5,300人，失踪人数估计可能高达50,000人，许多家庭仍在继续寻找亲人。

body.en:
Families in Venezuela are still searching for the remains of their loved ones, lost amid the rubble of flattened apartment buildings that line the coast of La Guaira, the region worst-hit by twin earthquakes on 24 June.

Government officials say the death toll has surpassed 5,300, though estimates of the number still missing could be as high as 50,000.

The BBC's Latin America correspondent Will Grant visited towns in La Guaira after the tremors first hit, and returned to find families continuing their search for loved ones a month on.
body.zh: 委内瑞拉的家庭仍在寻找亲人的遗骸，他们在拉瓜伊拉海岸的公寓楼被夷为平地的废墟中失踪，该地区是 6 月 24 日两次地震中受灾最严重的地区。 政府官员表示，死亡人数已超过 5,300 人，但估计仍然失踪的人数可能高达 50,000 人。 BBC 拉丁美洲记者威尔·格兰特 (Will Grant) 在第一次地震发生后走访了拉瓜伊拉 (La Guaira) 的城镇，回来后发现家人在一个月后仍在继续寻找亲人。

reflection.en: The ongoing search for loved ones a month after the Venezuela earthquakes highlights the profound grief and enduring pain that natural disasters inflict. In such moments of deep sorrow, we cling to the promise that Yahweh will one day wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. This hope reminds us that even in the face of...
reflection.zh: 委内瑞拉地震发生一个月后，家庭仍在持续寻找亲人，这凸显了自然灾害所带来的深切悲痛和持久痛苦。在如此巨大的悲伤时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟的应许：有一天他将擦去所有的眼泪，死亡、悲哀、哭号和疼痛都将不再有。这个盼望提醒我们，即使面对压倒性的损失，也有一个未来，所有的苦难都将止息。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Urgent need for more security after physical attacks and abuse, say MPs’ staff
title.zh: 议员工作人员称，在遭受人身攻击和虐待后，迫切需要更多安保

summary.en: A survey of Members of Parliament's staff in Westminster revealed that half of them are experiencing clinical levels of psychological distress. Staffers are calling for immediate security enhancements following reports of physical attacks and numerous threatening calls and messages.
summary.zh: 一项针对威斯敏斯特议员工作人员的调查显示，半数工作人员正经历临床水平的心理困扰。在接到人身攻击和大量威胁电话及信息报告后，工作人员呼吁紧急加强安保。

body.en: Exclusive: Westminster survey finds one in two staffers experiencing clinical levels of psychological distress Staff employed by MPs are calling for urgently tightened security after reports of some being physically attacked and hundreds receiving threatening calls and messages. A survey of more than 500 MPs’ staff members found that 78% had received threatening communication and nearly one in three fear for their own safety or that of colleagues. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家：威斯敏斯特调查发现，二分之一的工作人员经历了临床水平的心理困扰。在有报道称，一些议员受到人身攻击，数百人收到威胁电话和信息后，议员们雇用的工作人员呼吁立即加强安全保障。对 500 多名议员工作人员的调查发现，78% 的人曾收到过威胁性通讯，近三分之一的人担心自己或同事的安全。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The intense pressure and abuse faced by public servants, leading to clinical psychological distress, reminds us that even those in service can feel overwhelmed to the point of despair. In such moments, the Apostle Paul's words offer solace, acknowledging that there are times when burdens feel "far beyond our ability to endure." Yahweh understands our limits...
reflection.zh: 公职人员所面临的巨大压力和虐待，导致临床水平的心理困扰，这提醒我们，即使是服务他人的人，也可能感到不堪重负，甚至绝望。在这样的时刻，使徒保罗的话语带来慰藉，承认有时重担会让人感到“力不能胜”。雅伟理解我们的极限，并与我们同在最深的挣扎中。

verse.textEn: We were under great pressure, far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired of life itself.
verse.textZh: 我们被压太重，力不能胜，甚至连活命的指望都绝了。

title.en: Houthi attacks raise fears of wider Middle East conflict and more global economic damage
title.zh: 胡塞武装袭击引发对中东冲突扩大和全球经济损害加剧的担忧

summary.en: The Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen has threatened to target Saudi vessels in a crucial shipping route, escalating fears of a broader Middle East conflict and increased global economic disruption.
summary.zh: 获得伊朗支持的也门胡塞武装威胁要袭击重要航运路线上的沙特船只，这加剧了人们对中东地区冲突扩大和全球经济破坏加剧的担忧。

body.en:
Yemen's Houthi fighters claim to have attacked shipping in the Red Sea - a move that threatens to further escalate the already volatile situation in the Middle East.

By forcing ships to turn back from the narrow Bab El Mandeb strait, they have threatened to choke off the main maritime route from Europe to Asia.

It comes as US-Iran strikes continue and while a deal to develop Saudi Arabia's nuclear industry prompts fears of an arms race.

So far, 2026 is sadly proving to be one of the more violent years for parts of the Middle East.

For 13 consecutive nights, US Central Command (Centcom) has carried out air strikes on Iranian targets.

"Iranian military command centers, drone storage facilities, communication networks, coastal surveillance sites, and maritime capabilities to further diminish the threat Iran poses to civilian mariners and commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz," Centcom said in a statement on Thursday night.

The Gulf Arab states, in normal times a haven of low-crime tranquility and minimal taxation, are having to learn to live with constant attacks from their well-armed neighbour across the water: the Islamic Republic of Iran.

And now the Iran-backed Houthis of Yemen have entered the fray, after a 2022 ceasefire with neighbouring Saudi Arabia appeared to have broken down.

Two Saudi vessels were hit by missiles in the Red Sea this week , while the Houthis claim to have turned back 10 others after warning ships to avoid Saudi ports, disrupting shipping passing through the strategic Bab El Mandeb Strait that links the southern end of the Red Sea with the Indian Ocean.

This matters because, on top of the ongoing disruption to global energy and fertiliser supplies caused by Iran effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz , it is a further obstacle to vital maritime trade that will soon impact the global economy.

Saudi Arabia has been trying to distance itself from the Iran-US war and has been largely spared the Iranian drone and ballistic missile attacks that have rained down this month on Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan.

With the Strait of Hormuz closed, the Saudis have been able to partially mitigate the disruption to their oil exports by shipping millions of barrels a day through the East-West Pipeline that traverses the entire breadth of their huge country, from the oilfields of Eastern Province to the Red Sea export terminal at Yanbu' Al-Bahr.

From there, they have been able to ship oil in bulk to customers in Asia using tankers that depart south, past Yemen and that Bab El Mandeb Strait, and out into the open Indian Ocean.

But not anymore - at least not while the Houthis are threatening vessels that pass by their coast.

US President Donald Trump has vowed to "take care of the Houthis" but that has not worked before -...
body.zh: 也门胡塞武装声称袭击了红海航运，此举有可能使中东本已动荡的局势进一步升级。 通过迫使船只从狭窄的曼德海峡返回，他们威胁要切断从欧洲到亚洲的主要海上航线。 在此之际，美国和伊朗的袭击仍在继续，而发展沙特阿拉伯核工业的协议引发了人们对军备竞赛的担忧。 令人遗憾的是，到目前为止，2026 年对于中东部分地区来说是最暴力的一年。 连续13晚，美国中央司令部（Centcom）对伊朗目标进行了空袭。 中央司令部在周四晚间的一份声明中表示：“伊朗军事指挥中心、无人机储存设施、通信网络、沿海监视站点和海上能力将进一步减少伊朗对穿越霍尔木兹海峡的民用海员和商船构成的威胁。” 海湾阿拉伯国家在正常情况下是低犯罪率、宁静的避风港和最低税收的避风港，但现在却不得不学会忍受来自水对岸装备精良的邻国伊朗伊斯兰共和国的不断袭击。 现在，在 2022 年与邻国沙特阿拉伯达成的停火似乎破裂后，伊朗支持的也门胡塞武装也加入了战斗。 本周，两艘沙特船只在红海遭到导弹袭击，而胡塞武装则声称，在警告船只避开沙特港口、扰乱通过连接红海南端与印度洋的战略性曼德海峡的航运后，已击退了另外 10 艘船只。 这很重要，因为除了伊朗有效关闭霍尔木兹海峡造成的全球能源和化肥供应持续中断之外，这还进一步阻碍了重要的海上贸易，并将很快影响全球经济。 沙特阿拉伯一直试图与伊朗和美国的战争保持距离，并且基本上没有受到伊朗无人机和弹道导弹本月对巴林、科威特和约旦的袭击。 随着霍尔木兹海峡的关闭，沙特通过东西向管道每天运输数百万桶石油，从而部分缓解了对其石油出口的干扰。该管道横贯整个国家，从东部省的油田到延布巴赫尔的红海出口码头。 从那里，他们能够使用油轮向亚洲批量运输石油，油轮向南出发，经过也门和曼德海峡，进入开阔的印度洋。 但现在不再是了——至少在胡塞武装威胁经过其海岸的船只时不再如此。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普发誓要“对付胡塞武装”，但这之前并没有奏效——……

reflection.en: The escalating threats in vital shipping routes raise understandable concerns about wider conflict and economic instability. In times of such global uncertainty and fear, Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, a constant help in trouble. This offers a steadfast hope that we can turn to a higher power for solace and stability amidst...
reflection.zh: 航运要道上不断升级的威胁，引发了人们对更广泛冲突和经济不稳定的担忧。在这样的全球不确定和恐惧时期，诗篇46:1提醒我们，雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。这提供了一个坚定的盼望，即在动荡中我们可以转向更高的力量寻求慰藉和稳定。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: Watch: Driver dressed as Spider-Man whisks man in a wheelchair across busy road
title.zh: 视频：蜘蛛侠装扮司机助轮椅男士过马路

summary.en: Footage from a traffic junction captured a driver dressed as Spider-Man helping a man in a wheelchair cross a busy highway.
summary.zh: 交通路口监控录像捕捉到一名打扮成蜘蛛侠的司机帮助一名坐轮椅的男子穿过繁忙高速公路的瞬间。

body.en:
A driver dressed as Spider-Man was seen helping a man in a wheelchair cross a busy road in the US.

Christopher Hellenthal was on his way back from a superhero-themed event and jumped in to help moments before the lights at the junction changed.

The Jonesboro Police Department, in the state of Arkansas, shared the moment captured on traffic camera footage, thanking Hellenthal for his actions.
body.zh: 有人看到一名装扮成蜘蛛侠的司机帮助一名坐在轮椅上的男子穿过美国一条繁忙的道路。 克里斯托弗·海伦塔尔 (Christopher Hellenthal) 正在从一场超级英雄主题活动回来的路上，在路口信号灯变亮之前跳出来帮忙。 阿肯色州琼斯伯勒警察局分享了交通摄像头捕捉到的这一时刻，感谢海伦塔尔的行动。

reflection.en: The unexpected kindness of a driver dressed as Spider-Man, assisting a man in a wheelchair across a busy road, beautifully illustrates the command to love our neighbor. This simple act reminds us that compassion often involves practical, selfless help for those around us, reflecting Yahweh's call to care for one another.
reflection.zh: 一位打扮成蜘蛛侠的司机出人意料地帮助一名坐轮椅的男子穿过繁忙的马路，这美好地诠释了爱邻如己的诫命。这一简单的举动提醒我们，怜悯之心常常意味着为身边有需要的人提供实际、无私的帮助，这正回应了雅伟要我们彼此关爱的呼召。

verse.textEn: Love your neighbor as yourself.
verse.textZh: 要爱人如己。

title.en: Firefighters stand 'no chance' as European wildfires force tens of thousands to flee
title.zh: 消防员毫无胜算，欧洲野火迫使数万人逃离

summary.en: Wildfires in southern Europe have led to the deaths of three firefighters and forced tens of thousands of people to evacuate their homes. The region is currently experiencing a period of severe heat.
summary.zh: 欧洲南部发生的野火已导致三名消防员死亡，并迫使数万人撤离家园。该地区目前正经历一段严重的酷热天气。

body.en:
Wildfires sweeping through parts of Italy, France and Spain on Thursday forced thousands of people to flee blazes fanned by scorching temperatures and strong winds.

Thousands of tourists on France's southern Atlantic coast have been forced out of campsites and holiday homes while Spanish authorities ordered another town near Madrid to evacuate late Thursday because of an out-of-control forest fire.

Three firefighters have been killed as southern Europe endures more severe heat, with temperatures topping 40C in some areas.

The total area of land burnt so far this year in European Union countries is the second largest on record, according to satellite data from the European Forest Fire Information System.

"The gendarmes came and knocked on every door, the fire was about 500 metres away — we grabbed some things and left," said Patrick Martineau, a 69-year-old resident of Le Porge, south of the French city of Bordeaux.

In Sicily, around 6,000 firefighters, forest guards and civil protection officers battled dozens of fires, some raging for several days, across the Italian island. One firefighter died after falling ill while battling the flames, the interior minister said.

Around Bordeaux, more than 20,000 people — mostly tourists in campsites and holiday lets — have been evacuated since Wednesday, as a fire ravaged a seaside pine forest.

"We're dealing with a very dense stand of closely packed pines," firefighter captain Wilfried Schneider told the Agence France-Presse news agency, describing a fire of "rare" intensity.

"We were on the beach and they told us to go back to the campsite to collect our things," said Belgian tourist Elke Urbain.

"We're not afraid because everyone is taking care of us, but we're sad for the people here."

Skies over Le Porge turned orange as smoke rose from charred and crackling pine trees, while helicopters made repeated runs over evacuated neighbourhoods.

Fires in 2022 damaged 30,000 hectares of the same forest, forcing some 50,000 people to be evacuated.

Fires are breaking out faster because of climate change caused by the burning of oil, coal and gas. European droughts are now more severe, climatologists from the World Weather Attribution group said in a study published on Thursday.

Across the border in Spain, authorities ordered 3,500 people in a town west of Madrid to leave their homes late Thursday because of a forest fire burning out of control.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump said a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia depends on the kingdom recognising Israel — casting uncertainty over the agreement just the day after it was signed.

Saudi Arabia has long resisted joining the Abraham Accords , under which several Arab states established ties with Israel. The kingdom has long rejected joining the accords in the absence of a pathway toward Palestinian statehood.

The civilian nuclear deal announced on Thursday had appeared to be a major win for the Saudis, especially coming as Trump wages war on Iran in large part over concerns about the country's own atomic program.

But Trump threw a spanner into the works with his post on his Truth Social network saying the Saudi deal "will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords".

The White House said that the Saudis knew the deal was contingent on recognising Israel, although it was not mentioned when the deal was announced.

"The president is always the final dealmaker, as you know," White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters, adding that the Abraham Accords were "something that he feels very strongly about and has spoken about it in the past and will continue to uphold".

She said the US would "continue to have those conversations with our Saudi counterparts" to finalise a deal including recognition of Israel.

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said recognition by Saudi Arabia, a regional power and home to Islam's holiest sites, would mark a "historic leap" forward for peace in the Middle East.

Leavitt said she did not know of any calls between Trump and Netanyahu following the announcement of the Saudi agreement.

Should it go through, the deal to establish a civilian nuclear program in Saudi Arabia would generate billions of dollars for US companies, but with Trump's latest announcement, it was unclear whether it would ever see the light of day.

HA Hellyer, a senior associate fellow at the United Kingdom-based think tank the Royal United Services Institute for Defence and Security Studies, said if the US "tries to force normalisation on Riyadh, it's not likely to work out very well".

"Would Saudi decide to do a complete 180 on what it has declared for the past three years, or 30 years? Quite dubious," he said.

Critics have also insisted that the deal could precipitate a nuclear race in a region already battered by war.

One provision would potentially see US companies build a uranium enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia, The Wall Street Journal reported.

title.en: The US' $166 billion refund comes with a much bigger cost

summary.en: Trump's willingness to use tariffs to create persistent uncertainty signals a greater economic and legal danger.

body.en:
An Australian clothing company, Nashie, recently received a six-figure refund from the US government, including 6 per cent interest, for tariffs it had paid on US imports. It’s just one of thousands of businesses reclaiming tariffs imposed on what President Donald Trump called "Liberation Day".

Of the roughly US$166 billion (AU$237 billion) due to be refunded, more than US$85 billion (AU$121 billion) has already been returned to businesses.

But while a US Supreme Court ruling in February reversed the tariffs, much of the economic and political damage, and perhaps some of the Trump administration’s gains, will be hard to undo.

Trump’s April 2025 tariffs relied on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), a 1977 law that lets presidents respond to extraordinary foreign threats — yet never mentions the word "tariff".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

On 20 February 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled in a 6-3 decision that IEEPA did not authorise tariffs — under the Constitution, only Congress has the power to impose taxes and duties.

The decision placed an important limit on the president’s power to impose tariffs. But it did not end Trump’s tariff policy, which was, from the beginning, designed to buy time to rewrite US trade relations with the rest of the world.

Trump responded with a temporary 10 per cent global tariff, which expires on 24 July after the statutory 150-day limit.

Trump has also pursued more targeted tariffs under laws dealing with unfair trade practices, national security and anti-slavery claims.

These require investigations into foreign trade practices and lengthy procedures, which slow the process and also create a record that can be scrutinised in court.

The US Trade Representative’s findings on alleged forced labour have prepared the ground for a 12.5 per cent tariff on exports from 54 countries, including Australia, China, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, starting on 24 July 2026.

So while the Supreme Court closed one legal door, the Trump administration was already preparing to walk through another. And it has bought itself yet more time.

The refunds paid out contributed to a US$120 billion (AU$171 billion) federal deficit this June, in sharp contrast to the US$27 billion (AU$38 billion) surplus in June 2025.

That said, the US$166 billion (AU$236 billion) being paid out is not a fine. Much of it is money the government collected without legal authority and must now return. This is real money, but it’s less than 2 per cent of the projected 2026 federal government spending.

title.en: US-Saudi nuclear deal: How will it impact Middle East, US-Iran war?
title.zh: 美国-沙特核协议：将如何影响中东和美伊战争？

summary.en: Critics warn that a potential US-Saudi nuclear deal could ignite a nuclear arms race in the Middle East, causing concern among US allies like Israel and the UAE. Reports suggest the US may be reconsidering aspects of the agreement.
summary.zh: 批评人士警告称，一项潜在的美国与沙特核协议可能在中东引发核军备竞赛，这已引起美国盟友如以色列和阿联酋的不安。有报道指出，美国可能正在重新考虑该协议的某些方面。

body.en:
Critics say the US-Saudi deal could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. It's certainly not making US allies, like Israel and the UAE, happy. And reports suggest the US may already be backtracking on the deal.

After new statements by US President Donald Trump on Thursday morning, it is still unclear whether a controversial new deal with Saudi Arabia that allows the Middle Eastern autocracy to establish a civilian nuclear program will go ahead.

Trump said the deal could only progress if Saudi Arabia normalized diplomatic relations with Israel. In the recent past, the Saudi government has repeatedly stated it would only do this if the Israelis make genuine moves toward establishing a Palestinian state. With the current Israeli government, that is unlikely to happen.

The deal must also be voted on by the US Congress and there's been backlash already, with critics saying it could set off a nuclear arms race in the Middle East.

One of the main reasons experts are so worried is that in several years' time, the deal, as it stands now, may let the Saudis enrich their own uranium. The more uranium is enriched, the more it could potentially be diverted to make weapons. And in the past Saudi Arabian ruler Mohammed bin Salman has said that if Iran produces a nuclear bomb, then Saudi Arabia would need to have one too. 

The majority of the approximately 38 countries with civilian nuclear energy programs don't enrich uranium. Instead they import it.

The US-Saudi deal also has regional implications, especially because it seems to have been formulated in a far less rigorous way than similar deals.

The less strict deal the US has made with Saudi Arabia is likely to upset the  United Arab Emirates , who often compete with the Saudis for geopolitical influence.

The UAE already has a nuclear power plant, Barakah, as a result of arrangements made with the Americans back in 2009. 

As with almost all of the 26 nuclear cooperation agreements the US has, the UAE's deal also included what's known as an "additional protocol" signed with the International Atomic Energy Agency, or IAEA. This means the IAEA can thoroughly inspect all nuclear facilities. The UAE also agreed to forgo uranium enrichment.

The Saudi deal is bilateral only — that is, just between the US and the Saudis and doesn't include the IAEA — and the Saudis may eventually be allowed to enrich their own uranium.

title.en: US strikes on southern Iran infrastructure widen war
title.zh: 美国对伊朗南部基础设施的打击使战争扩大

summary.en: The United States has conducted new strikes on infrastructure in southern Iran, including tunnels and bridges, further inland from the Strait of Hormuz. These actions suggest a potential shift in Washington's strategy regarding Iran, raising concerns about a broader conflict.
summary.zh: 美国对伊朗南部基础设施，包括霍尔木兹海峡内陆的隧道和桥梁，进行了新的打击。这些行动可能表明华盛顿对伊朗的策略正在发生转变，引发了对冲突扩大的担忧。

body.en:
The latest US strikes on tunnels, bridges and other infrastructure further inland from the Strait of Hormuz could indicate that Washington is shifting gears in Iran.

With the US and Iran back at war following a prolonged but shaky truce , the latest US strikes seem to be less focused on Iran's coastal installations and maritime targets in the Strait of Hormuz .

Iranian media and local officials have reported  strikes on bridges, tunnels, roads, rail infrastructure, power facilities and desalination plants in southern Iran over the past week.

Hormozgan province, just north of the Strait of Hormuz, has been hit especially hard.

According to Iranian media, six bridges in Khamir county were struck early on Friday, July 17.

Hours later, more reports followed of attacks on two tunnels and two more bridges in Hormozgan. At least eight people were reported killed in the bridge strikes.

The US military also appears to have conducted the strikes in a very deliberate pattern. In the first wave, bridges west and north of provincial capital Bandar Abbas were hit.

In a second wave, another bridge to the east, one to the north and two tunnels north of the city were damaged. Alongside that, part of the railway west of Bandar Abbas was also struck.

Shukria Bradoost, an international security analyst at Virginia Tech in the US, told DW that the main US objective remains the same as before.

"The American goal in attacking southern Iran is to reopen the Strait of Hormuz," she said.

However, she noted that Washington is trying to do more than remove direct military threats to shipping .

The US military is destroying the infrastructure that could help Iran rebuild, reposition or sustain military pressure in the area, she added, noting that this was the reason that bridges, roads and rail lines have become targets.

She also warned that Washington could move to take control the strategic Kharg Island, the home of Iran's main oil export terminal, in its push to remove the wider threat to Hormuz.

The US has so far refrained from targeting energy facilities on the island, home to Iran's main oil export terminal, said Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East.

"Naturally, the island is valuable as long as its oil facilities remain operational and undamaged," he told DW. "But the key question is whether the United States is seeking to seize Kharg militarily or whether, through repeated attacks, it is pursuing what could be described as a political seizure of the island."

reflection.en: News of escalating military actions reminds us of the profound truth that violence often begets more violence. Yahweh's word warns that those who live by the sword risk perishing by it, urging us to consider the long-term consequences of widening conflict.

title.en: Trump's refugee policy: Only white South Africans welcome?
title.zh: 特朗普的难民政策：只欢迎南非白人？

summary.en: A report indicates that while US refugee spending has increased, the primary beneficiaries are white South Africans, with individuals from crisis-stricken nations often denied entry. Experts suggest this policy damages the credibility of US refugee aid.
summary.zh: 一份报告指出，尽管美国在难民方面的支出有所增加，但主要受益者是南非白人，而来自饱受危机困扰国家的人们却常常被拒绝入境。专家认为，这项政策损害了美国难民援助的公信力。

body.en:
Trump is spending more money on refugees, but it's mostly white South Africans who benefit. People from crisis-stricken countries are being denied entry. Experts say the credibility of US refugee aid has been damaged.

The US government cited an "unforeseen emergency" in South Africa  as the reason the refugee program would be expanded. However, only white minority South Africans — who are allegedly being persecuted on racial grounds in their country — would be granted refugee status . The Trump administration has repeatedly claimed that there is an ongoing genocide against white Afrikaners , allegations the South African government strongly denies .

Experts also say there is no statistical evidence of increased crime targeting white farmers. 

For Oscar van Heerden, a research fellow at the Center for African Diplomacy and Leadership at the University of Johannesburg, this is based on a distorted understanding intended to "undermine South Africa's moral authority on the international stage — by equating South Africa with the State of Israel."

Since the start of the war in Gaza , South Africa has been among Israel's harshest critics. In late 2023, Pretoria filed a lawsuit with the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague against the Israeli government over allegations of genocide against the Palestinian population in Gaza.

The case stems from Israel’s response to the October 7, 2023 terrorist attacks carried out by Hamas,  which is considered a terrorist organization by the US, the EU and others, and other militant Islamist groups. Israel denies the allegations of genocide and invokes its right to self-defense. It could take years before a final decision is reached.

Essentially, according to van Heerden, US President Donald Trump is saying: How can a country like South Africa bring Israel before the ICJ for alleged genocide against the Palestinians in the Gaza Strip when the South Africans themselves are committing genocide against white South Africans?

"He has this twisted notion in his head that he will convince the world that, after the Mandela years, we [South Africa] no longer have any moral authority in the world," he told DW.

Through an emergency order in 2025, Trump made it possible for members of white minority groups from South Africa to enter and resettle in the US . The US State Department's decision now calls for raising the annual cap on refugee admissions for the 2026 fiscal year from 7,500 to 17,500. The additional 10,000 spots are reserved exclusively for white South Africans. The State Department estimates that the expanded program would cost around $100 million (€87 million).

title.en: Zelenskyy has faced years of war. Now comes a test from within
title.zh: 泽连斯基已身经多年战火，如今面临内部考验

summary.en: The news reports that Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is facing growing political strains and internal unrest, highlighted by a recent military shake-up, as the war against Russia continues.
summary.zh: 新闻报道，随着对俄罗斯的战争持续，乌克兰总统泽连斯基正面临日益增长的政治压力和内部动荡，最近的军事改组凸显了这一点。

body.en:
Nearly four and a half years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of his country, Ukrainian President Volodymr Zelenskyy faces one of his toughest domestic political challenges yet.

In the past week, the biggest protests Zelenskyy's leadership has ever seen swept through Kyiv as frustrations over how to win the war against their eastern neighbour spilled over. Thousands of young people took to the streets to protest contentious recruitment methods and decry the allegations of corruption swirling around the administration.

In an effort to placate the demonstrators, Zelenskyy replaced his army chief Oleksandr Syrsky on Wednesday. The 60-year-old veteran commander had been the focus of the unrest following the removal of a younger, reform-minded defence minister.

That minister, 35-year-old Mykhailo Fedorov , was demoted by Zelenskyy just six months into the job. It has been reported that Syrsky may have encouraged Zelenskyy to get rid of the tech-savvy junior and has now himself been replaced by Mykhailo Drapatyi as head of the military.

Protesters demand Fedorov be reinstated, but Zelenskyy has said he will not reappoint him to the defence ministry, offering him a range of other roles instead. Federov has rejected them, saying no other role can impact the course of the war as much as his former one.

Demonstrations are likely to continue as a result of the deadlock, although discussions are expected to carry on between the men.

Analysts say Zelenskyy's leadership could be in trouble, especially given it comes after former prime minister Yulia Svyrydenko was replaced earlier this month.

Ukrainian opposition MP Oleksiy Goncharenko told  the SBS World News Weekly podcast  that Zelenskyy's position is "very weakened" amid ongoing corruption scandals, and the rotation of political appointments suggests Zelenskyy is trying to shore up his position.

However, Iryna Skubii, senior researcher in Ukrainian studies at the University of Melbourne, told SBS News that what may appear to be a crisis from the outside reflects "how democracy works" in Ukraine.

"It's how civil society illustrates what they want from political leadership at this time, and political leadership listened to them and made this decision accordingly," she said.

Ukraine has been subject to Russian aggression since the illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014. The conflict escalated when Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. title.en: Blocked by censors, China's animal lovers take fight against abuse offline and overseas
title.zh: 遭审查阻挠，中国动物爱好者将反虐待斗争转至线下和海外

summary.en: The killing of a dog and her puppies in Guangdong, China, has provoked widespread outrage both within the country and internationally. Animal welfare advocates, facing censorship, have taken their campaign against animal abuse offline and sought support overseas.
summary.zh: 中国广东省一只狗及其幼崽被杀害的事件，在中国国内外引发了广泛的愤怒。面对审查，动物福利倡导者已将他们的反虐待动物运动转至线下并寻求海外支持。

body.en:
When videos showing the horrific killing of a stray dog and her puppies sparked outrage on the Chinese internet in June, Beijing's censorship machine kicked into action.

But what was unusual this time was that it pitted the shocked and angry voices against authorities who said they were concerned about the four boys involved, all of them younger than 14.

China's Communist Party regime tightly controls media and the internet to suppress criticism of the state and to manage public anger. But in this case authorities cited the age of the boys as they urged people to withhold their comments and scrubbed social media posts about the incident.

"We urge the public not to disseminate related information, to reject cyberbullying, and to work together to create a good environment for the growth of minors," reads an official statement.

But the restrictions only seemed to spur the outcry. China's animal lovers have now taken their fight offline and abroad, even putting up billboards in New York to drum up support.

In China, posts about the incident are still drawing thousands of comments across social media, three weeks after the incident. There is shock, anger and sorrow, as well as demands for laws against animal cruelty, which China currently does not have.

Disturbing footage showing the boys in the city of Jieyang, Guangdong province, hitting three puppies with sticks before setting their mother on fire emerged online at the end of June. The boys were seen laughing as the dog, named Wang Wang, burned.

Jieyang authorities said last month that the boys would not face criminal charges and would instead be sent to a "specialised school", but did not elaborate.

Some reports suggest the boys filmed themselves and uploaded the video online, but police have not commented on that. Censors have tried to block the video to protect the boys' identity, although some people argue that it should stay.

Their identities have not been revealed, but snippets of the video with their faces visible continue to circulate online. There are also unverified posts claiming to be close-ups of the boys' faces, raising the risk of other children being wrongly identified.

Countries around the world restrict information about child offenders or set a high bar for identifying them.

For instance, media coverage and public access to juvenile court documents are often restricted to minimise psychological harm caused by undue publicity.

In this case, Chinese authorities have not completely banned the discussion yet. Keywords such as "Wang Wang" and "animal protection" came up as trending search terms on Monday, but posts related to them started to disappear towards the end of this week. Some users have also reported that their ability to share others' posts has been restricted.

summary.en: A food delivery rider has won China's highest literary award, highlighting a growing trend of laborers engaging in creative writing. summary.zh: 一名外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖，这凸显了劳动者从事创意写作的日益增长的趋势。这一现象揭示了数亿建设现代中国的劳动者——从扫街工人到工厂员工和货物运输者——丰富的内心世界。

body.en: A food delivery rider has won the country’s highest literary award. It is part of a growing trend for writing by labourers The hundreds of millions who have built modern China from the ground up – sweeping its streets, labouring in its factories and ferrying its goods – are often overlooked. But they refuse to go unheard. Last week, a food delivery rider won China’s top literary award . Wang Jibing, 56, first caught attention when a poem about his experiences went viral in 2022. The following year, Hu Anyan’s memoir , I Deliver Parcels in Beijing, became a bestseller. In the early 20th century, Chinese intellectuals sought to capture the harsh realities of working-class lives. But it was under Mao Zedong that the idea of writing by as well as about the masses became reality, with labourers encouraged to take up the pen. In an era when the party tried to govern the language even of diaries and personal letters, the parameters of style and content were strict, and this enthusiasm swiftly diminished after Mao. title.en: Can India become the next semiconductor hub after Taiwan?
title.zh: 印度能否成为继台湾之后的下一个半导体中心？

summary.en: India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.
summary.zh: 随着主要工业强国寻求将供应链多元化，不再只依赖台湾，印度正投入数十亿美元建设国内半导体产业。

body.en:
India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.

More than 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductor chips are made in Taiwan , an island at the center of ongoing rivalry between the US and China .

Any disruption to Taiwan's chip industry would likely send shockwaves through the global economy, with modern semiconductors used to make everything from smartphones and electric vehicles (EVs) to aircraft and military systems .

During the COVID-19 pandemic, chip shortages forced automakers to halt production — exposing how dependent the world had become on a handful of manufacturers in East Asia.

The result has been a global race to build more resilient semiconductor supply chains. The US, Japan, South Korea and also the EU have all launched multi-billion-dollar programs to attract chipmakers.

India is now mounting its biggest push yet to become part of that network and enter the global arena as the next electronics powerhouse.

Last week, the Indian government approved a $13.2 billion (€11.4 billion) semiconductor program labeled Semicon 2.0. The project builds on the $9 billion India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) launched in 2021 and aims to develop the entire chip ecosystem — from chip design and fabrication to advanced packaging, specialty materials, equipment manufacturing and workforce training. 

Thousands of engineers working for companies such as Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and Texas Instruments already design some of the world's most sophisticated chips from research centers in the Indian cities of Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Noida.

But analysts warn India has been lagging behind in large-scale manufacturing. In the semiconductor industry,  this is the area that brings both economic value and strategic importance.

"India already has the expertise to design sophisticated semiconductor chips," said V Kamakoti, director of the Indian Institute of Technology in the city of Madras.

"Indian engineers working for both domestic companies and multinational firms have successfully designed and delivered complex chips," Kamakoti told DW. "The bigger challenge is manufacturing them."

So far, India's progress has been concentrated in chip packaging and testing rather than manufacturing the chips themselves.

Kamakoti said the next step is building a domestic fabrication ecosystem that can turn those design strengths into large-scale production.

Micron Technology, a US memory chip maker, Kaynes Semicon and CG Semi, two Indian semiconductor assembly and packaging companies, have begun commercial production under the first phase of India's semiconductor program.

title.en: 'Strong concerns': Australia meets with China following ballistic missile test
title.zh: “强烈关切”：澳大利亚在中国弹道导弹试验后与中方会晤

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

title.en: Chinese, Philippine personnel clash in the South China Sea
title.zh: 中国和菲律宾人员在南海发生冲突

summary.en: China Coast Guard and Philippine Navy personnel clashed in the South China Sea, with Chinese personnel using wooden batons against Philippine sailors. One Philippine sailor reportedly sustained a serious head injury during the incident.
summary.zh: 7月20日，中国海警人员与菲律宾海军人员在南海发生冲突，中国海警人员使用木棍攻击菲律宾水兵。据菲律宾当局称，一名菲律宾水兵在冲突中头部受重伤。

title.en: Police allege Socceroos star tested positive for cocaine after speeding twice
title.zh: 警方称澳大利亚足球明星在两次超速后检测出可卡因呈阳性

summary.en: Police said Volpato was travelling nearly 50km/h over the speed limit when he was pulled over.

body.en:
Socceroos star Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine, after police stopped him while speeding over a bridge.

The 22-year-old, who represented Australia at the World Cup , was caught speeding twice overnight, NSW Police said on Friday.

Driving a BMW, Volpato was allegedly clocked at 109 km/h — nearly 50 km/h over the designated speed limit — when police stopped him on Sydney's Anzac Bridge at 1.10am on Friday.

He was subjected to a roadside drug test which allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine, police said in a statement.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Volpato had earlier been stopped at 11.05pm on Thursday, police said, for travelling between 86 and 94km/h in a 60 zone.

Volpato returned a negative result when he was given the initial roadside breath test.

Volpato, who plays club football for Italian side Sassuolo, made three appearances for the Socceroos at the World Cup.

He made headlines shortly before the tournament when he switched his international allegiance from Italy to Australia.

Volpato, who was born and raised in Sydney and played his junior football at Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney before moving overseas, represented Italy at U19 and U20 level.

The 22-year-old, who has scored seven goals in his three seasons with Sassuolo after two seasons with fellow Serie A club Roma, said in March he was "waiting for Italy" to select him for the senior side, who subsequently failed to qualify for the World Cup.

Deadly H5 bird flu appears to have reached Queensland's coastline for the first time as detections in wild seabirds across Australia climb to 17, sparking fresh warnings for vulnerable wildlife.

A deceased petrel found on Moreton Island returned an initial positive result for highly pathogenic H5 avian influenza at the Queensland government's Biosecurity Sciences Laboratory.

Samples have been sent to CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness for confirmatory testing.

Invasive Species Council policy director Carol Booth said the arrival of H5 bird flu in Queensland should alarm anybody concerned about Australia's native animals.

"Bird flu has now reached Queensland's coastline, and that should concern every Australian who cares about our wildlife," Booth said.

"We can't stop this virus, but we can boost the capacity of wildlife to survive and recover from outbreaks."

Australia reported its first case of H5 bird flu on 20 June, and there are now 17 confirmed detections of the serious H5 strain in wild seabirds — 10 in Western Australia, five in South Australia and two in NSW.

Booth said surveillance efforts were working but warned they would not be enough once the virus hit vulnerable species.

"Finding cases is only the first step — once this disease reaches vulnerable wildlife populations, surveillance won't prevent the devastating impacts we've seen overseas," she said.

"Millions of wild birds and marine mammals have died, and unless we do everything we can to strengthen the resilience of at-risk populations, there's every reason to fear Australia could face similar losses."

There have been no detections in poultry and no evidence of large-scale deaths in any animals in Queensland, according to the Department of Primary Industries.

"It is safe to continue to eat chicken meat or eggs, and I would encourage Queenslanders to purchase these products as they normally would," said Queensland's Primary Industries Minister Tony Perrett.

Queensland's Chief Veterinary Officer, Allison Crook, said the suspected positive result was anticipated and the state was well prepared.

"We have known that a H5 bird flu detection in Queensland was a matter of when, not if," Crook said.

"This suspect positive result has not impacted our poultry sector or native wildlife and we are continuing our enhanced passive surveillance program throughout the state and would encourage the community and industry to continue to be vigilant."

Booth continued to urge the federal government to back a major "wildlife resilience" package to help species withstand bird flu and other threats.

body.en:
Nearly five million Australians have been urged to stay vigilant for scams after a cyber attack on Origin Energy saw customer data accessed and disclosed.

Origin — Australia's largest energy retailer, with roughly 4.8 million customer accounts across electricity, gas, LPG and internet services — confirmed that names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and account information were all potentially viewed in the breach.

It said on Thursday it was working to understand how many of its customers were affected.

Also potentially exposed were the last four digits of credit cards and the last three digits of bank accounts.

That combination of data has raised the risk of follow-up scams, particularly phishing attempts that use real account details to appear more convincing.

Phishing scams involve fraudsters posing as a trusted organisation, often via email or text, to trick people into handing over personal details, passwords, or banking information.

But experts warn phishing may not be the only thing customers need to worry about.

New guidance from the company has urged customers to stay alert for scam emails and texts, designed to deceive people into providing their personal details.

"These fake emails often include a corporate logo and look like they've come from a legitimate company," Origin said.

Anyone who believes they've received a scam email is encouraged to report it to Scamwatch .

Origin has recommended customers keep a strong, unique password for their account and never share it with anyone, stressing it will never ask for a password over the phone or via email.

If a scam email arrives, the company's advice is to not click links, open attachments or forward it on, but to report it directly.

To tell a genuine email or text apart from a fake, Origin says to check for a suspicious sender address, spelling mistakes or bad grammar, and where any links actually lead.

"We've seen scam websites posing under originnergy.com.au so look carefully at the website address," Origin said, adding that the only safe way to pay a bill was via their website or the Origin app.

The company has also flagged fake job offers, and bogus calls or emails requesting orders or parts from people posing as Origin procurement staff, as scams to watch for.

Some experts say the breach is another example of a major company failing to handle a data incident well, and are calling for tough accountability standards for essential service providers.

The government has hit back at blanket new 12.5 per cent tariffs imposed by the United States on Australian goods, which came into effect on Friday.

The new permanent levy replaces a temporary 10 per cent tariff due to expire at the same time and is part of what the US claims is an effort to tackle the global issue of "forced labour" in supply chains.

Whilst the government insists its handling of forced labour and modern slavery is top-tier, one expert has said Australia's protections are greatly lacking, while another has suggested that Australia is a victim of Trump's tensions with China in this scenario.

Australian Trade Minister Don Farrell has called for the tariff measures to be reversed, telling SBS News that they are "unjustified" and "inconsistent" with existing free-trade agreements with the US.

"Australia's measures to combat forced labour and modern slavery are among the strongest in the world, and we are recognised globally, including in the US, for our leadership."

Almost all goods sent to the US will be affected at the specific direction of US President Donald Trump.

However, roughly 70 per cent of Australian exports are already covered under existing tariff exemptions, although it is not clear whether these exemptions will roll over under the new, higher rate.

Australia has increased its exports to the United States by 67 per cent since April 2025, when a blanket 10 per cent global tariff was applied on Trump's so-called "Liberation Day", Farrell said.

Primary exports to the US include beef, gold, wine, medical products, and various mining resources, the volume of which has increased dramatically, Farrell said, bringing the total value of the trading relationship to $1.32 trillion.

"Our largest exports to the United States continue to get into the United States tariff-free. What are they? It's beef, it's gold, and it's copper," Farrell told a press conference on Friday.

Australia is among 41 other economies the US trade department claims have failed to "impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced with forced labor". These include Brazil, China, Egypt, India, Israel, Japan, Norway, Russia, and Singapore.

Other regions, which the US claims have also failed to "enforce" forced labour prohibitions, face a 10 per cent tariff. These include Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and Mexico.

title.en: Not a 'one off spike': Why higher petrol prices are set to return
title.zh: 并非“一次性飙升”：为何汽油价格将卷土重来

summary.en: Multiple factors are expected to push up prices at the bowser, as markets also ramp up expectations for another rate hike.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Petrol prices are expected to rise once again, which could cause a crunch at the bowser for Australians already feeling the pinch.

While Australia's resilient labour market continues to be a bright spot in the nation's economy, including the addition of more than 76,000 jobs in June, dark clouds are gathering on the horizon.

After the Australian Bureau of Statistics released another strong labour force report on Thursday, bonds traders ratcheted up expectations that the Reserve Bank will raise interest rates for a fourth time in 2026.

The market is now full priced in for a rate hike by Christmas. A few weeks ago it was a 50-50 bet.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Renewed hostilities in the Middle East have sent oil prices rising again and threaten to add fresh inflationary pressures to the economy.

While June quarter inflation data next week will be crucial to the RBA's next rates decision in August, the figures could already be dated by the time they are released.

Brent crude oil prices have risen from $US72 ($103) a barrel to more than $US96 ($138) a barrel in recent weeks.

As a rule of thumb, each dollar higher the benchmark oil price results in about a cent per litre increase in petrol prices at the bowser.

Along with an extra 16c a litre added to fuel prices from 2 August because of the full resumption of the federal excise , commuters could soon be looking at petrol prices above $2 a litre once more.

Australians might have to become accustomed to higher fuel prices sticking around, said economists at National Australia Bank.

"Recent developments in the Middle East show that the cost shock looks set to be less of a one-off spike and instead something that proves more grinding and protracted," they said in a research note.

Although jobs growth has remained robust, at 4.4 per cent the unemployment rate is higher than the RBA's June quarter forecast of 4.2 per cent, implying that the labour market is weaker than had been expected.

While higher oil prices risk pushing inflation higher, they also pose risks for growth, said Commonwealth Bank head of Australian economics Belinda Allen.

Victoria's economy is leading the way down, where the state's unemployment rate climbed to 5.1 per cent.

"That's a warning sign that both the Allan and Albanese governments are failing to create the economic conditions businesses need to invest, grow and create jobs," said federal opposition employment spokesperson Jane Hume.

title.en: Australia’s winter wonderland is becoming increasingly reliant on a backup plan

body.en:
As the sun rises over Mount Buller in Victoria's High Country, the hum of snow guns echoes across the mountain, blanketing ski runs in artificial snow.

As winters become less predictable, operators are investing heavily in snowmaking technology, effectively an insurance policy keeping lifts turning and visitors coming when natural snowfall falls short.

With little natural snow falling until 3 July, one of the slowest starts to winter in decades, several resorts still managed to turn lifts on the traditional June long weekend opening thanks to artificial snowmaking — even if only thin stripes of beginner's terrain were open.

Among them was Mount Buller, which has invested $17 million in snowmaking in the past 25 years.

The resort now operates more than 300 snow guns across almost 80km of ski runs, which can generally operate only at a wet-bulb temperature of -2C or below.

Mount Buller also has five snow factories — shipping container-like buildings capable of producing snow around the clock, regardless of temperature.

"Snowmaking has progressively become more and more significant around the world because it smooths out the variability from season to season," Mount Buller spokesperson Rhylla Morgan told SBS News.

"We haven't had many of those big snow events yet. There have only been a handful so far this season, so snowmaking helps us fill in those gaps.

"It allows us to maintain snow cover across the ski area and steadily build that base, which has enabled us to progressively open more terrain and keep our guests skiing and snowboarding."

Morgan said snowmaking technology — which is both water-and energy-intensive — had improved significantly in the decades since its introduction, allowing resorts to produce higher-quality snow more efficiently.

"The technology has really become very finessed; there are amazing companies around the world working to improve that every year," she said.

Resorts also rely on "snow farming" to extend their seasons by creating snow stockpiles in south-facing and shaded areas, which are then groomed to top up runs.

She said Australia's ski industry — which supports more than 22,000 jobs and contributes billions of dollars to the economy — was continuously adapting to the changing climate.

While snowmaking has helped resorts cope with poor natural conditions, it hasn't changed the weather.

After an early July dump of snow, the Spencers Creek measuring site — considered the most reliable site for natural snow depth in NSW — recorded a depth of 68cm on 21 July. A good year would exceed a metre.

body.en:
A cyberattack on Origin Energy has included unauthorised access and disclosure of customer data, the energy giant says, a day after it revealed it was caught up in the breach.

The Sydney-based company said on Thursday it was working to understand how many of its almost five million customers were affected by the privacy incursion.

Names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and account information could all have been viewed in the breach, Origin said in an ASX statement.

Also at risk were the last four digits of credit cards, or the last three digits of bank accounts.

Origin chief executive Frank Calabria apologised to customers and said the company was working to contact those affected.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The company has set up a contact number and "additional resources to help manage our response to this incident".

"One of our key priorities is taking action to secure our systems and ensure no further unauthorised access," Calabria said.

"We are working with independent cyber experts to support Origin, and that work is continuing alongside the work of authorities."

The company continued to engage with federal cyber and information agencies on the incident as well as police, according to the statement.

Origin, which has 4.8 million customer accounts in Australia and provides electricity, natural gas, LPG and internet services, said on Wednesday it did not believe the data obtained included credit card or bank details.

Griffith University's Graeme Hughes, an expert on business and consumer issues, said the breach was unlikely to cause cases of payment fraud but marked a "social engineering problem".

"The last four digits for a card, a date of birth, and an authentic billing history are the exact trust signals a businesses uses to verify itself over the phone," Hughes told AAP.

"That makes an unsolicited call about an energy account far more convincing than it should be.

"If comparable Australian breaches have taught us anything, the confirmed scope (of the breach) usually widens rather than narrows."

The breach represents the country's most high-profile cyber incident since Partnered Health, owned by private equity firm Quadrant, said earlier in July that its medical records were breached clinics in Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra.

In 2025, airline Qantas said it had customer data published by cybercriminals, while telco giant Optus and health insurer Medibank were hit in attacks in 2022 that sparked cyber-resilience laws.

Pauline Hanson has denied downplaying the scourge of domestic violence after labelling the issue a "two-way street", as advocates warn the politician's framing is dangerous.

The One Nation leader is facing criticism from experts over comments she made about domestic violence , which Hanson claimed had been taken out of context by media outlets.

"Domestic violence is wrong, but it's also a two-way street," she told 4BC radio on Wednesday.

"Domestic violence is a scourge, but look ... if you're not in a house where you feel safe ... then you shouldn't put up with it.

"If these women are getting abused by men out there, then don't put up with it."

Sex Discrimination Commissioner Anna Cody said she was sorry Hanson had also experienced domestic violence, with the national crisis affecting one in four women and girls in Australia, but criticised her message.

"Any suggestion that victim-survivors share the blame is harmful, wrong, and dangerous," she said.

"Domestic violence is never the responsibility of the person experiencing it. Just this month, two women and two girls have been allegedly murdered."

Women's Community Shelters chief executive Annabelle Daniel said the evidence was clear that domestic   and family violence is a gendered issue.

"With Australia in the grip of a housing affordability crisis, it's nowhere near as easy as 'just leave'," she said.

"Affordable housing, professional support and community inclusion prevent women becoming homeless because of domestic and family violence in the first place and support their recovery after abuse."

In a Facebook post on Thursday, Hanson said there is a "concerted effort by some in the media to constantly take my comments out of context".

"But some within rival media decided to use only a few quotes and made out that I downplayed domestic violence," she said.

The One Nation leader linked the declining trust in media to recently announced job cuts at Nine newspapers.

"I'm growing less tolerant of many journalists within the [mainstream media] and so too are the public," she said.

Hanson also walked back a number of comments on different issues, including paid parental leave and increasing defence spending to 5 per cent of the nation's economic output.
